subject.title: Execution anti-drift guards: artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and no-idle-after-green

question: Should OpenClaw add a core enforced execution-progress contract for artifact-gated status, escalation timers, and post-green follow-through, and if so what is the narrow MVP boundary?
rationale: The request fits reliability goals, but it adds new enforcement policy, persistence, config/flag surface, timers, and telemetry that can change user-visible agent behavior and cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require a scoped MVP that reuses runner/diagnostic events, SQLite-owned state, and measured telemetry before enabling enforcement.

options.title: Split into concrete smaller bugs
options.body: Track only proven failures against existing loop, stale-run, stuck-session, and timeout detectors until live traces justify broad artifact-gated enforcement.

options.title: Decline broad enforcement
options.body: Close the direction as too policy-heavy for core and continue relying on existing loop detection, stuck-session diagnostics, and operator monitoring.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core guardrail design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design tracker and require a scoped MVP that reuses runner/diagnostic events, SQLite-owned state, and measured telemetry before enabling enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available routing candidate from the current guardrail and idle-timeout history, though ownership is shared with adjacent loop-detection contributors.
